\caption{What the test shows in hazard terms and what it could have missed, for all ground nearest a settlement with a water-side name (\MatchWetPct{} of the cells) and for the ground within 500\,m of such a settlement. All quantities are exploratory (amendments 2, 3 and 5 to 10, or not planned, footnote a); the pre-specified result is in Table~\ref{tab:si-comparisons}. Contributions are on the scale of the pooled $R$, that is, the change in the Brier score of all cells divided by the terrain gain. $^{a}$~The increments on this ground (amendment 2) re-expressed on the pooled scale (not planned). $^{b}$~Effect injected on a latent indicator of truly water-related names, drawn with the misreading rates measured against recorded etymologies. $^{c}$~Leaks the outcome by construction (the cell itself is left out): an upper bound, not a possible reading of names. $^{d}$~Known for \RecurCovPct{} of the cells; zero with an indicator elsewhere. $^{e}$~AOIs and cells that radar can assess; built-up land and seasonal water are excluded. $^{f}$~Base models fixed; no-effect reference: the mean increment of reassigned names with the regional composition rebuilt (amendment 8); in parentheses, Monte Carlo 95\,\% intervals over the simulated replicates (\PlasRepsA{} each). Bounds with other references are in Tables~\STabEightBounds{} and \STabNineBounds{} of the Supplement. $^{g}$~Within 500\,m, intervals from a pairs cluster bootstrap over location groups (2,000 replicates); other odds ratios have cluster-robust intervals.}\label{tab:hazard}
